questions.question: When a bus starts suddenly, the passengers are pushed back. This is an example of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's first law.**__

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Newton’s first law of motion: It is also called the law of inertia. Inertia is the ability of a body by virtue of which it opposes a change.
 
• According to Newton’s first law of motion, an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• The inertia of rest: When a body is in rest, it will remain at rest until we apply an external force to move it. This property is called inertia of rest.
 
• The inertia of motion: When a body is in a uniform motion, it will remain in motion until we apply an external force to stop it. This property is called inertia of motion.

EXPLANATION__:

__
 
• When a bus suddenly starts moving, the passengers fall backward due to the law of inertia of rest or **1st law of Newton**.
 
• Because the body was in the state of rest and when the bus suddenly starts moving the lower body tends to be in motion, but the upper body still remains in a state of rest due to which it feels a jerk and falls backward. Hence option 1 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Laws of Motion given by Newton are as follows:

 
 

 Law of Motion
 Statement
 
 

 First Law of motion 
 An object continues to remain at rest or in a state of uniform motion along a straight line unless an external unbalanced force acts on it.
 
 

 The second law of motion
 The rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force and the change of momentum occurs in the direction of the force.
 
 

 Third law of motion 
 Every action force has an equal and opposite reaction force which acts simultaneously.

questions.question: In a uniform circular motion:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speed is constant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Circular motion **is a movement of an object along the circumference of a circle or rotation along a circular path.
 
• The distance and displacement are different at every instance at any particular point of time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• **While the speed is a scalar quantity, in uniform motion, it remains constant**.
 
• As, Velocity is a vector quantity, and the direction of movement changes continuously, **velocity changes continuously**.
 
• Due to this, the object is in accelerated motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

**About the Circular Motion:**

 
• As the direction of the **velocity changes at every instant**, it is an accelerated motion.
 
• During the motion, the particle repeats it's paths along the same trajectory.
 
• Thus the motion is periodic.

**Uniform Circular Motion:**

 
• During circular motion, if the speed of the period remains constant, it is a Uniform Circular Motion. **Hence option 4 is correct**.

• Sulphur trioxide is a chemical compound with the formula SO₃.
 
• Sulfur dioxide in air directly oxidizes to Sulphur trioxide extremely slowly:
 
 
• SO₂ + 1 over 2O₂ → SO₃

questions.question: What is the role of ribosomes of a polysome?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Translate the mRNA into proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes of a Polysome **

 
 
• The **cellular organelles** known as** ribosomes** are made up of **proteins and rRNA**.
 
• Before they bind to mRNA, they are **present free in the cytoplasm**.
 
• Multiple ribosomes that are joined to the** mRNA **and contain developing **polypeptide chains** are known as** polysomes**.
 
• A **polysome** is made up of** **all the ribosomes that translate a **single mRNA into many polypeptides (Proteins)** at once.
 
• The **coding portion of mRNA**, which is transported by **multiple **ribosomes, forms a **polysome**.
 
• The presence of** so much mRNA in cells **is due to the **ability of multiple ribosomes** to participate in an **mRNA's function**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prokaryotic, eukaryotic, and membrane-bound polrsomes** all have different structures of multiple ribosomes also known as **polyribosomes**.
 
• **Bacterial polysomes** are found in** double-row formations in prokaryotic cells**, and ribosomes are in touch with one another within smaller subunits.
 
• Planar double row** polysomes and densely packed 3D helices**, which are similar to that of prokaryotic polysomes, are also present in** eukaryotic cells**.
 
• **Polysomal profiling** is a method for** **determining the level of gene expression by monitoring polysome activity. 
 
• Translation is stopped using polysomal profiling, and **sucrose gradient **is then used to separate the resultant cells so that they may be collected by centrifugation.

questions.question: Electrical energy used during a month is expressed in terms of 'units'. Here one unit means
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__**:**

__
 
• Electrical energy: The energy that is derived from the flow of electric charge is called electrical energy.

 
 
• The SI unit of electrical energy is Joule.
 
 
 
• Kilowatt-hour: It is the unit of energy and is equal to the energy consumed in the circuit at the rate of 1 kilowatt for 1 hour.
 
 
• The commercial unit of electrical energy is a kilowatt-hour (kWh).
 
 
 
• Electric Power: The rate at which electrical energy is consumed in a circuit is called electric power.
 
 
• SI unit is the watt.
 
• One Kilowatt is equal to 1000 watts.
 
 

EXPLANATION__**:**

 
• The **commercial unit of electrical energy** is a **kilowatt-hour (kWh)**. Therefore option 2 is correct.

 
• The commercial unit of electric energy is kilowatt or the Board of Trade (B.O.T) unit.
 
• One kilowatt-hour is defined as the electric energy consumed by the appliance of 1 kilowatt in one hour and it is also called one unit of energy.

1 kilowatt-hour = 1 kilowatt × 1 hours = 1000 watt × 3600 s

1 kWh = 3600000 joules = 3.6 × 10⁶ J = 1 Unit of energy

questions.question: A ray of light is incident on a very thin prism, the infractive index of the material of the prism is 1.6. The deviation of the ray of light is 6°. Find the angle of the prism.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Dispersion of light: The phenomenon in which a white light ray when falls on a prism get separated into its component colors is called dispersion of light.

 
• Different colors of different wavelengths experience different degrees of deviation and hence when put through refraction, white light splits into its constituent colors.
 
• When light rays fall on the prism then there is a deviation in the path of the ray after refraction through the prism.
 
• For a thin prism deviation angle is very small.
 
• The deviation angle (δ) for a thin prism of prism angle A is given by:

δ = (n - 1) A

Where n is the refractive index of the Prism

CALCULATION__:

Given - Angle of deviation (δ) = 6° and Refractive Index (n) = 1.6

 
• The deviation angle (δ) for a thin prism of prism angle A is given by:

⇒ δ = (n - 1) A

⇒ 6 = (1.6 - 1) A = 0.6 A

Rightarrow A = (6)/({0.6)} = 10^circ

So option 2 is correct.

__
 
• **A vacuole **is a **membrane-bound cell organelle**.
 
• In **animal cells**, **vacuoles **are generally **small **and **help sequester waste products**.
 
• In **plant cells**, vacuoles **help maintain water balance**.
 
• **Sometimes **a **single vacuole **can take **up most of the interior space **of the **plant cell**.

 __

• **Cytosols**__
 __
 
• The **cytosol **is the **liquid medium contained **within a cell.
 
• The **cytosol **is a **component of the cytoplasm**.
 
 
 
• **Golgi apparatus**__
 
 
• The **Golgi apparatus**, also known as the **Golgi complex**, **Golgi body**, or simply the **Golgi**, is an **organelle **found in **most eukaryotic cells**.

questions.question: Which of the following elements shows a catenation property like carbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Si.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Catenation** refers to the ability of an element to **form bonds **with other atoms of the same element, resulting in the formation of **long chains or rings**.
 
• **Carbon** is well known for its **catenation property, **which is why it can form a vast number of organic compounds. 
 
• **Silicon** (Si), shows a catenation property like carbon.
 
• This is because silicon has** four valence electrons**, like carbon, and can form **covalent bonds** with other silicon atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neon** (Ne) **does not** show catenation property as it is a **noble gas** and does not readily form bonds with other atoms.
 
• **Oxygen** (O) can form **limited catenation**, but not to the same extent as carbon or silicon.
 
 
• This is because oxygen has only **two valence electrons** and can only form **two covalent bonds** with other oxygen atoms.
 
 
 
• **Potassium** (K) is a metal and **does not **show catenation property as metals typically** lose electrons** to form positive ions and do not form covalent bonds with other atoms of the same element.

questions.question: Oleo gum resin (Asafoetida) can be obtained from:

options.text: dried latex from the stem of ferula
dried latex from the roots of mango tree
dried latex from the banana leaves
dried latex from the tap root of ferula

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dried latex from the tap root of ferula**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The spice **asafoetida** is the **dried latex** (gum oleoresin) exuded from the living underground rhizome or tap root of several species of **Ferula** which is a **perennial herb **(1 to 1.5 m high).
 
• It is **greyish-white** when fresh, darkening with age to yellow, red and eventually brown.
 
• It is **sold in blocks** or **pieces** as gum and more frequently as a fine yellow powder, sometimes crystalline or granulated.

• It is used in modern **herbalism** in the treatment of hysteria, some nervous conditions, bronchitis, asthma and whooping cough.

questions.question: Which one of the following tissues provides tensile strength against bending and swaying?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Plant tissues are classified into **two main groups:**

 
 
• **Meristematic tissue** - capacity to d**ivide actively throughout its life**, induces growth, responsible for the formation of new organs, heals injured parts.
 
• **Permanent tissue** - completely developed, lost the ability of division.
 
 
 
• The meristematic tissues **divide and differentiate to form the permanent tissues.**
 
• **Permanent tissues** can again be of 2 types - simple and complex.

**Simple permanent tissue** - 

 
• **Parenchyma**

 
 
• Simple permanent **living storage tissue**
 
• It is composed of **thin-walled polyhedral, isodiametric living cells** with** sufficient cytoplasm and one or more nuclei**
 
• **Most widely distributed** tissue in the plant body
 
• **Major part of ground tissues** in plants, where other tissues like vascular tissues are embedded
 
• **Cell wall is uniformly thin** and **made up of cellulose**
 
• Cells** store substances** like food, water, secretory and excretory products
 
• Performs** functions like photosynthesis, storage and secretion**
 
• Makes up the chloroplast-laden mesophyll of leaves, cortex, pith of stems and roots, forms the soft tissues of fruits
 
• They are also contained in xylem and phloem as transfer cells and as the bundle sheaths that surround the vascular strands
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma**
 
 
• It is a** simple permanent living mechanical tissue**
 
• Found in the **hypodermal regions of dicot stem, leaf and fruit walls**
 
• Cell wall is **unevenly thickened** with **cellulose and pectin**
 
• The strength of the tissue results from these **thickened cell walls** and the** longitudinal interlocking of the cells**
 
• **Provides mechanical support **__to growing parts of **plants such as young stem, petiole of leaf**
 
• It is __**extremely plastic**__—the **cells can extend** and thus adjust to increased growth of the organ
 
• **Constitutes the ridges and angles of stems and commonly borders the veins** in eudicot leaves
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma**
 __
 
• It is a **simple permanent dead mechanical tissue** at maturity
 
• Heavily **thickened secondary walls containing lignin**
 
• The cells are** ****rigid and non-stretchable**__
 
• Usually **found in nongrowing regions** of plant bodies, such as the bark or mature stems
 
• Consists of** long, narrow cells with thick and lignified cell walls**
 
• __**Provides mechanical support**__ to the plant organs
 
• Two main types occur: fibres and sclereids
 
 

__
 
• **Aerenchyma**

 
 
• **Modification of the parenchyma** to form a **spongy tissue**
 
• It **creates spaces or air channels in the leaves**, stems and roots of some plants
 
• It **allows exchange of gases** between the shoot and the root
 
• **Found in aquatic plants** like lotus and water hyacinth as these cells help the plant float on water
 
 

**Complex permanent tissue** - 

 
• **Xylem**

 
 
• It **transports water and minerals** from roots to stem and leaves

questions.question: How do humans acclimatise at high altitudes where atmospheric pressure is low for normal breathing?

options.text: By decreasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate
By increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate
By increasing white blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acclimatisation**

 
 
• **Acclimatisation** is the l**ong-term adaptation to high altitude**, which is primarily carried on **by an increase in red blood cell production and capillary tissue perfusion**.
 
• At high altitudes, acclimatisation typically **takes 1-3 days**.
 
• The b**ody undergoes a number of adaptations** that enable it to **function with less oxygen **at high altitudes, such as:
 
 
• the** depth of breathing increases **or by increasing breathing rate.
 
• Increased **pulmonary arterial pressure "forces" blood into areas of the lung** that are typically not used when breathing at sea level.
 
• The **body creates more red blood cells to transport oxygen**, as well as more of an enzyme. 
 
• By decreasing the **binding affinity of haemoglobin**.
 
 
 
• In order to reduce the **effects of altitude sickness and to balance out increased urination, it's critical to stay hydrated during acclimatisation**.
 
• Despite acclimation, the **heart rate and ventilation rate both rise when at rest, **whereas the heart rate falls when ** at its highest degree of activity due to the release of oxygen from haemoglobin to the body's tissues**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Altitude Sickness**

 
 
• At sea level, **there are around 21% more oxygen** molecules than usual.
 
• While the **concentration does not change with the increase in altitude but the amount of oxygen molecules per breath and the atmospheric pressure decreases**.
 
• At **12,000 feet (3,658 metres)**, there are around **40% less oxygen **molecules in each breath.
 
• Even while at rest, **your breathing rate needs to increase for the body to receive enough oxygen**.
 
• Continued exposure to **higher altitudes without enough acclimatisation might result in very serious, even fatal illnesses**.

questions.question:
Which of the given statements is correct for a conservative force field

(p) The total mechanical energy is conserved.

(q) The work done around a closed path is zero.

(r) Gain in kinetic energy = Loss in potential energy.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Conservative force: A force is conservative if the work done by the force in displacing an object from one point to another point is independent of the path followed by the object and depends only on the endpoints.
 
• Electrostatic forces, gravitational forces, elastic forces, magnetic forces, etc and are examples of conservative forces.

 
• Non-conservative forces: A force is said to be non-conservative if work done by or against the force in moving a body from one position to another, depends on the path followed between these two positions.
 
• Examples: Frictional force, Viscous force, Airdrag, etc.

EXPLANATION__:​

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5352446eb65e10d74cfbb9f4ac2c20d3a00fd036413930010e6fdd4bc32569b3.png] **__

 
• Suppose a particle starts at A and a **force Fₑₓₜ is acting on it**. The particle is moved around the loop using the same force, Fₑₓₜ
 
• Suppose the particle eventually **ends up at A itself** then the entire **displacement of the particle is zero** which means the **total work done is zero**.
 
• A total work of one zero means there is no expenditure of energy which means the **total energy is conserved**. Hence statement p is correct
 
• The **total displacement of a particle** in a **closed loop is zero**, which means the **total work done is zero**. Hence statement q is correct.
 
• The total mechanical energy of a system is given by 

⇒ Total energy = Potential Energy + Kinetic energy

 
• From the statement p,** **it is clear that if the** total work done is zero **it means the **energy is conserved.**
 
• Which means** Gain in kinetic energy = Loss in Potential Energy**. Hence option r is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is essential for DNA Synthesis and cell division?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the course of its lifetime, a cell undergoes **continuous cell cycles** to** regenerate its number and give rise to daughter cells that retain the characteristics of the parent cells.**
 
• This is important for the **growth, repair, regeneration, and maintenance of a tissue or cellular population. **
 
• The cell cycle comprises** two growth phases, a synthesis phase, and a cell division phase.**
 
• **Cell division** refers to the **biological phenomenon** whereby a cell undergoes a** complex series of physiological, anatomical, and biochemical alterations to produce daughter cells. **
 
• Cell division is of two major types, i.e., **mitosis and meiosis. **
 
• **Mitosis** occurs in all the** autosomal cells **and results in the formation of **two identical daughter cells.**
 
• **Meiosis** occurs **only in the germinal cells or the gametes** **(sperm in males and ovum in females)** to produce **four daughter cells. **
 
• The process of cell division is preceded by the phase of DNA synthesis.
 
• **DNA synthesis is the phase of a cell cycle that requires replication and synthesis of genetic material, i.e., DNA.**
 
• The **DNA of the parent cell serves as a template **for the **synthesis** of **new DNA** as the genetic material of the daughter cell. 
 
• A complex machinery of enzyme-protein complexes assists in carrying out this process. 
 
• **Folic acid **or** vitamin B9 **is an important component of these stages of the cell cycle. 
 
• This is so because** folic acid converts to tetrahydrofolate** that functions as a **coenzyme for the synthesis of DNA.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Folic acid **also plays a role in **erythrocyte formation, energy metabolism,** as well as the** conversion of homocysteine to methionine.**
 
• Thus, it prevents anemia, aids tissue growth and cellular proliferation along with hastening metabolic processes. 
 
• **Vitamin D** is important for the **intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphorus, strengthening of bone density, and lowering of blood pressure.**
 
• **Vitamin E** is an **anti-oxidant** that **prevents skin and other tissue damage due to free radicals.**
 
• **Vitamin K **has predominant roles in **blood clotting (prothrombin is a Vitamin-K dependent protein) and in increasing bone density (associated with a protein called osteocalcin).**

questions.question: Phytoplankton, small sea-dwelling organisms, belong to which trophic level of the food web?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary producers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phytoplankton**, also known as **microalgae**, are similar to **terrestrial plants **in that they contain **chlorophyll **and **require sunlight **in order to **live and grow**.
 
• **Most phytoplankton **is **buoyant **and **floats **in the **upper part of the ocean**, where **sunlight penetrates the water**.
 
• **Autotrophs **or **primary producers **are **organisms **that acquire **their energy from sunlight **and **materials from nonliving sources**.
 
• **Algae**, **higher plants**, and **some bacteria **and protists are important **autotrophs in running waters**.
 
• **Heterotrophs **obtain **energy **and **materials **by **consuming living **or **dead organic matter**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary consumers **make up the **second trophic level**. They are also called **herbivores**. They eat **primary producers**—**plants or algae**—and **nothing else**. For example, a **grasshopper **living in the **Everglades **is **a primary consumer**.
 
• The **organisms **that **eat the primary consumers **are **meat eaters **(carnivores) and are **called secondary consumers**. The **secondary consumers **tend to be **larger and fewer in number**. This **continues **on, all the way up to the **top of the food chain**.
 
• **Decomposers **feed on **dead things**: **dead plant **materials such as **leaf litter **and **wood, animal carcasses, and faeces**. They perform a **valuable service as Earth's cleanup crew**. Without **decomposers**, **dead leaves**, **dead insects**, and **dead animals **would **pile up everywhere.**

• A cyclotron is a device used to accelerated positively charged particles (like α -particles, deuterons etc) to acquire enough energy to carry out nuclear disintegration, etc. 
 
• It is based on the fact that the electric field accelerates a charged particle and the magnetic field keeps it revolving in circular orbits of constant frequency.

 Rightarrow f = frac{{qB}}{{2pi m}}

m = frac{{{m_o}}}{{sqrt {1 - frac{{{v²}}}{{{c²}}}} }}
Where mo = rest mass of the particle, v = velocity of charged particle and c = speed of light** **

 
• 
 
• At high velocities, the cyclotron frequency ( {f = frac{{qB}}{{2pi m}}} ) will decrease due to the increase in mass. Therefore statement 1 is correct.
 
• This will throw the particles out of resonance with the oscillating field. That is, as the ions reach the gap between the dees, the polarity of the dees is not reversed at that instant. Consequently, the ions are not accelerated further.

 
• Electrons cannot be accelerated in a cyclotron. A large increase in their energy increases their velocity to a very large extent. This throws the electrons out of step with the oscillating field.

• **Bromine gas (Br2)**: Bromine gas is also a diatomic molecule, comprising two bromine atoms bonded together.
 
• **Balanced Equation:**
 
• To balance the equation, we need to ensure that the number of atoms of each element is the same on **both sides of the equation**.
 
• In this case, we have two hydrogen atoms on the left side (2H) and two hydrogen atoms on the right side (2H), as well as two bromine atoms on the left side (Br2) and two bromine atoms on the right side (2HBr).
 
• Thus, the equation is balanced.
